title: Peruvian-Style Beef and Tomato Stir-Fry with Chips and Rice
summary: Strips of sirloin are seared hard in a smoking wok, then tossed with charred onion, pepper and juicy tomatoes in a soy-lime sauce and spooned over crisp oven chips with rice on the side.
equipment: wok or large heavy frying pan (30 cm)

ingredients.item: floury potatoes (such as Maris Piper or Russet), cut into 1 cm chips
fine sea salt or table salt
beef sirloin, trimmed, cut across the grain into strips 1 cm thick and 5 cm long
large red onion, cut into 1.5 cm wedges
yellow pepper, cut into 1 cm strips
green chilli, seeded and thinly sliced
ripe plum tomatoes, cut into 1.5 cm wedges

ingredients.note: check the label: some soy sauces list alcohol

steps.title: Roast the chips
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (fan 200°C). Rinse the chips, dry them very well in a towel, toss with the chip oil and spread in a single layer over the 2 lined trays. Roast for 35-40 min, turning once and swapping the trays halfway, until golden and crisp, then toss with the chip salt. Rinsing removes surface starch and thorough drying stops them steaming, so they crisp properly.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: While the chips roast, rinse the rice until the water runs clear and put it in the saucepan with the 450 ml water. Bring to the boil, cover, turn the heat to its lowest setting and cook for 15 min. Leave covered off the heat for 10 min, then fluff with a fork; the resting time lets steam finish the grains evenly.

steps.title: Get organised
steps.text: Pat the beef dry and toss with the pepper. Mix the soy sauce, cider vinegar and lime juice in a small bowl. Everything needs to be lined up by the hob, because once the wok is hot the cooking takes only minutes.

steps.title: Sear in two batches
steps.text: Heat the wok over high heat until it smokes, add 1 tbsp of the stir-fry oil and half the beef in one layer. Leave it for 1 min to brown, turn and cook 1 min more, then move it to the plate. Repeat with another 1 tbsp oil and the rest of the beef; small batches keep the wok hot so the meat sears rather than stews.

steps.title: Char the vegetables
steps.text: Add the last 1 tbsp oil with the onion and yellow pepper and stir-fry for 2 min until charred at the edges but still crisp. Toss in the garlic and chilli for 30 s, just long enough to smell fragrant without burning.

steps.title: Bring it together
steps.text: Pour in the soy mixture and let it bubble for 30 s, then add the tomatoes and the beef with its juices. Toss for 1-2 min until the tomatoes just soften and the sauce coats everything. Check the thickest strip of beef reads at least 63°C, tossing 30 s more if needed, then take off the heat and leave for 3 min.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pile the chips on a platter and spoon the beef, vegetables and sauce over the top so the chips soak up some of the juices. Scatter with coriander and serve with the rice.

tips: A common mistake is adding all the beef at once; it cools the wok and the meat turns grey, so always sear in two batches.
Dry the chips thoroughly after rinsing, as any water left on them stops them crisping.
Add the tomatoes last and cook them only briefly so they keep their shape.
Check the label on your soy sauce, since brands differ.
storage: Refrigerate leftover beef and rice separately within 2 hours for up to 3 days; reheat both until piping hot (74°C). The chips are best eaten fresh but can be re-crisped in a hot oven.
